Probably not with unaided eyes, despite the Moon being geometrically above the horizon.

It is a very thin waning crescent—about **11.4% illuminated**—only **39.4° from the Sun**. At **12:21 in bright daylight**, the Moon is just **18.2° high**, where atmospheric haze and extinction further reduce contrast. Its position is roughly **41° west/right of the Sun** and **16° lower**, in the south-southwest.

Under exceptionally transparent Icelandic skies, an experienced observer might barely detect it after carefully locating the exact position, but for an ordinary observer I’d rate it **unlikely**. Binoculars would make it much easier, but only use them after ensuring the Sun is completely excluded from the field and cannot be swept across accidentally.
